Possibly, but this can't be confirmed yet. Hansen/UMD mapped about 13.5 ha of tree-cover loss in 2025 within the asset (3.91% of its 345.6 ha). Nearly all of it (98%) was forest in 2020 per JRC, and the MGAP 2021 map classes about 13.1 ha of the affected area as native forest, with 0.4 ha outside mapped forest and no planted forest.

Important limits:
- **Not yet corroborated.** 2025 is the last year of the series, so there is no later year to show the loss is persistent. The assessment is pending.
- **Loss is not necessarily deforestation.** Hansen counts any stand-replacing loss, including harvest, fire or storm damage, so land-use change isn't established.
- **Cause, legality and responsibility are unknown.** The evidence says nothing on these.

In short, there is a candidate native-forest loss of about 13.5 ha in 2025, but it can't yet be called deforestation. A later year of data is needed to corroborate it.
